absent: Numeric encodings of reboot type and mode, BOOT selectors, real-restart targets and CF9 safety default.
Bodies and contracts of ACPI reboot, EFI reboot, real-mode restart, IDT invalidate, native shutdown and crash shutdown, kernel restart and power-off helpers, and power-off feasibility check.
Layouts of machine operations, trusted-boot shared page, MAC region, e820 table, real-mode header and kexec control structures.
Semantics of DMI matching, reboot default and force flags, and crash NMI shootdown with callback registration.
Remainder of 64-bit relocate identity and virtual phases beyond the truncated fragment.
Construction of the kexec indirection list, control-page field offsets and preserve-context flag meanings.
Locking beyond interrupt-context prohibition and NMI coordination, and multiprocessor shutdown ordering.
Reset side effects of board fixup handlers beyond the port and config writes shown.

findings.text: Native machine operations supply defaults for halt, power off, restart, shutdown, emergency restart and optional crash shutdown, while public machine wrappers forward to the installed table and restart variants record an emergency flag before dispatch.

Trusted boot shutdown is exposed as one entry accepting a shutdown type; it returns early when the feature is off or page tables are absent, otherwise records the request, switches address spaces and enters firmware without returning.

Board-specific reboot correction has a default weak hook that does nothing and a 32-bit PCI override that walks a fixed table and runs the matched handler for each installed device unless in interrupt context.
A non-returning panic helper for non-dumping processors repeatedly runs the registered crash callback for current registers and relaxes the processor.

Early reboot initialization leaves configuration unchanged when an override is present, otherwise gives the DMI quirk table first priority and selects EFI reboot only when no quirk matches and firmware reports it required with runtime services enabled.

The 32-bit kexec trampoline saves caller state and control structures, disables interrupts, switches to supplied page tables with a fresh stack, executes identity-mapped code that normalizes control registers and flushes translation, swaps target pages via an indirection list, then either clears registers and returns or invokes the new image and supports a return path that restores tables, paging and saved state.

The 64-bit trampoline prologue preserves registers, invalidates descriptor tables, switches to kexec page tables, adjusts paging feature flags while saving the original value, records stack and control state plus flags and list pointer, establishes a control-page stack and jumps to identity mapping where it builds and loads debug descriptors before the truncated remainder.

The quirk table maps combinations of vendor, product, board and BIOS version patterns to forced PCI, BIOS or ACPI reboot selectors across many desktop, laptop, workstation, server and small-form systems, ending with an empty terminator.

Emergency virtualization teardown has an active variant that disables interrupts and either handles the local processor or triggers NMI-based peer shutdown when no crash IPI was issued, plus an empty variant doing nothing, paired with conditional versus empty NMI helpers.
Measurement regions ignore empty inputs, otherwise page-align start down and end up, append while capacity remains and fail fatally when the fixed table is full.

Sleep preparation has a memory-scanning variant that resets the region count, adds every RAM e820 entry and records the resume vector from the real-mode header, and an unsupported variant that faults unconditionally and reports failure.

The page swapper walks destination, indirection, completion and source tags encoded in low bits, masks entries to page bases, and performs a three-way copy through the supplied swap page for each source and destination pair.
The PCI fixup scan must return immediately when in interrupt context, preventing unsafe PCI access when invoked from emergency paths.

Each fixup entry stores numeric vendor and device values with a handler pointer, and the static table binds five PCI identities to warm or hard reset handlers, including one locally defined Intel bridge number.

Crash coordination keeps an integer for the crashing processor defaulting to negative one, a callback pointer for NMI handling, an atomic waiter count and an integer flag showing whether a crash IPI was issued.

Emergency restart runs an endless cycle over ACPI, keyboard controller, EFI, BIOS, safe and forced CF9 port and triple-fault methods, each step falling through to a defined successor, with pending EFI capsules forcing EFI, warm versus cold selection programmed to low memory, trusted shutdown first, and one retry of the original ACPI choice after keyboard attempts.

Trusted shutdown proceeds from enabled and page-table checks through optional S3 measurement preparation that may defer to normal handling, then records the type, switches to trusted tables, calls the firmware entry indirectly and halts forever if it returns.

Emergency reboot paths must avoid locks and tolerate inconsistent state, using NMIs for cross-processor coordination, bounded polling of the keyboard status bit with small delays, ordered CF9 port sequencing with warm versus cold encodings, and IDT invalidation followed by a breakpoint to force a triple fault.

Relocation runs with changing stacks and address spaces, requiring identity mapping, translation flushes and serialization, avoidance of stale pointers after table switches, and clearing of registers and return markers when prior context is not preserved.

Reboot hardware facts: keyboard status port 0x64 with busy mask 0x02 and reset value 0xfe, CF9 port 0xcf9 with enable and warm 0x06 versus cold 0x0E codes, fast reset port 0x92, PCI config ports 0xCF8 and 0xCFC, bridge config offset 0x44, low-memory flag at 0x472 with warm marker 0x1234, poll bound 0x10000 and retry count 10 with short microsecond delays.

Relocation facts: page-sized control and swap areas, tag values 1, 2, 4 and 8 for destination, indirection, completion and source, page-base mask 0xfffff000, 1024 words per page copy, normalized paging and protection feature bits, and flag-selected preserve versus discard behavior with zeroed return address when discarding.
